name: Zinc mouthwash (TheraBreath)

lead: Zinc mouthwashes such as TheraBreath combine zinc ions with other agents like chlorine dioxide and are sold to neutralise the volatile sulfur compounds that cause bad breath. People use them for fresher breath in close contact.

Zinc ions are described as binding the sulfur compounds and chlorine dioxide as oxidising them, which is the basis of the marketing. Published zinc research mostly concerns mouth ulcers and mucositis rather than breath, and no trial specific to this brand was found. Zinc used with chlorhexidine is reported to reduce its staining.

paras: It is used as a daily rinse after brushing, or before social occasions, often as part of a breath-focused routine alongside tongue cleaning and interdental cleaning.
The sources reviewed report no product-specific harms.

angle.text: Zinc rinses such as TheraBreath are used to neutralise the volatile sulfur compounds behind bad breath, aiming for fresher breath up close. Zinc has been studied for mouth sores, and no trial specific to this product's effect on breath was found.

lead: Zinc-containing mouthwashes, including the TheraBreath line marketed for bad breath, combine zinc ions with other agents such as chlorine dioxide to bind or neutralise the volatile sulphur compounds that cause oral malodour.[1] Wikipedia notes zinc is used with other antiseptics in rinses, and that zinc formulations with chlorhexidine stain less.[2][3]

Published research on zinc rinses mostly concerns mouth sores and mucositis rather than breath, and no trial specific to the TheraBreath product appears in the literature reviewed.[4][5][6][7] A 2025 dental review looked at cetylpyridinium chloride and zinc rinses together.[8]
infobox: Zinc salts, chlorine dioxide (in some products)

paras: Oral malodour is attributed mainly to volatile sulphur compounds produced by bacteria, and a study of dental-office workers measured their daily rise and fall.[1] Zinc rinses are marketed on the basis that zinc ions bind sulphur compounds; the sources reviewed do not report a trial testing this for the TheraBreath product.

A double-blind randomised trial compared zinc sulfate with chlorhexidine mouthwash for preventing chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis in leukaemia patients.[4] Two Iranian trials compared mouthwashes with and without zinc in erosive oral lichen planus and in aphthous stomatitis, in each case combined with steroids.[5][6] A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis found that the route of zinc administration determined efficacy for radiation-induced mucositis.[7] No studies found specifically on the TheraBreath product for halitosis.
Chlorhexidine rinses containing zinc are reported to stain teeth less than those without.[3] The sources reviewed do not describe product-specific adverse effects.
